chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from one of our companions, from Ja'far ibn Anbasa, from Abbad ibn Ziyad Al-Asadi, from Amr ibn Abi Al-Miqdam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him); and Ahmad ibn Muhammad Al-Asimi, from the one who narrated it to him, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad Al-Basri, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

In the letter of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) to Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'Do not give the woman authority in matters that exceed her own nature, for that is more favorable for her state, more relaxing for her mind, and more lasting for her beauty. Indeed, the woman is an aroma (delicate) and not a wrestling champion (strong/dominant). Do not let her soul surpass her honor, lower her gaze with your covering, restrain her with your veil, and do not incite her to intercede for others so that the one for whom she intercedes may incline against you along with her. Preserve a remnant of yourself from them, for restraining yourself from them while they see you as capable is better than them seeing you in a state of breaking apart.'

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Saeed, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad Al-Hasani, from Ali ibn Abdak, from Al-Hasan ibn Tariq ibn Nasih, from Al-Husayn ibn Ulwan, from Sa'd ibn Tariq, from Al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah, from the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), similar to it, except that he said: 'The Commander of the Faithful, may Allah's prayers be upon him, wrote this letter to his son Muhammad, may Allah be pleased with him.'

key_terms.بِحِجَابِكَ: With your veil; referring to seclusion or modesty
key_terms.بِسِتْرِكَ: With your covering; referring to modesty and protection
key_terms.حَالًا عَلَى انْكِسَارٍ: A state of breaking/submission; referring to weakness or loss of dignity
key_terms.ذُو اقْتِدَارٍ: Capable/Powerful; referring to strength and competence
key_terms.رَيْحَانَةٌ: Aroma; metaphor for delicacy and gentleness
key_terms.قَهْرَمَانَةٌ: Wrestling champion; metaphor for strength and dominance

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic advice regarding the balance of authority and delicacy in marriage?
ai.summary: This narration, transmitted through multiple chains in Al-Kafi, highlights the Shia concept of 'Rihana' (fragrance/delicacy) versus 'Qahramana' (dominance), advocating for a husband's dignified restraint rather than absolute control. It underscores the ethical responsibility of the husband to provide a protective 'hijab' (covering) for his wife, ensuring her modesty while preserving his own spiritual and emotional strength. This advice reflects the broader Shia jurisprudential emphasis on mutual rights and the husband's role as a guardian who balances authority with tenderness.
